rationale: Reviewed Cascade Health PPO Readmission Review Guideline and the medical records for index stay MR_07 (03/13/2026-07/04/2026) and readmission RM_07 (07/09/2026-07/19/2026). Gate: Cascade's review window is 30 days from prior discharge (RULE-Policy-Documents-Readmission-Payer-Guidelines-Cascade-Health-PPO-Readmission-Review-Guideline.docx-b4: 30 days from prior discharge), and the readmission occurred 5 days after index discharge (NOTE-Readmission-RM_07-readmission-RM_07.pdf-n125 p.120: 40F ... presented 5 days post-discharge...), so the readmission is in-scope. Cascade's Section B asks first whether the readmission diagnosis is the same as or clinically related to the condition treated during the prior stay (RULE-Policy-Documents-Readmission-Payer-Guidelines-Cascade-Health-PPO-Readmission-Review-Guideline.docx-B1). The readmission discharge summary explicitly documents recurrent bilateral pulmonary embolism and states this is the same class of thromboembolic disease driven by an underlying thrombophilia identified on the index stay (NOTE-Readmission-RM_07-readmission-RM_07.pdf-n125 p.120: Clinical Relationship: Index admission MR_07 ... Readmission RM_07 ... Recurrent bilateral PE ... same class of thromboembolic disease ... Underlying thrombophilia (D68.51) present on both admissions and drives the recurrence). Cascade's Section C exclusions list transfers, scheduled/staged admissions, SNF/LTAC/rehab discharges, AMA, etc.; none of those exclusions apply in this case (RULE-Policy-Documents-Readmission-Payer-Guidelines-Cascade-Health-PPO-Readmission-Review-Guideline.docx-C1). The index discharge is documented as 07/04/2026 (NOTE-Readmission-RM_07-index-MR_07.pdf-n955 p.838: Admit: 2026-03-13 Transfer: 2026-07-04), supporting the 5-day gap. Because (1) the readmission is within the 30-day window, (2) the readmission documentation explicitly ties the recurrent PE and right femoral DVT to the same thromboembolic disease/thrombophilia treated during MR_07, and (3) no exclusion in Section C applies, the readmission meets Cascade Health PPO's 'same or clinically related condition' criterion and is a Finding. Evidence cited: RULE-Policy-Documents-Readmission-Payer-Guidelines-Cascade-Health-PPO-Readmission-Review-Guideline.docx-b4 (review window), RULE-Policy-Documents-Readmission-Payer-Guidelines-Cascade-Health-PPO-Readmission-Review-Guideline.docx-B1 (same/related criterion), RULE-Policy-Documents-Readmission-Payer-Guidelines-Cascade-Health-PPO-Readmission-Review-Guideline.docx-C1 (exclusions), NOTE-Readmission-RM_07-readmission-RM_07.pdf-n125 (Clinical Relationship & hospital course summary, p.120), NOTE-Readmission-RM_07-index-MR_07.pdf-n955 (index discharge date, p.838).

Discharge summary completed and attested by the attending physician of record on 07/19/2026. This document serves as the authoritative discharge record for claim RM_07.

rationale_letter: Date: [Today's Date] To: Medical Records / Billing Office Re: Readmission claim RM_07 (Patient Isabella Chen-Rodriguez / MRN MRN-5827194) - Determination: Finding We completed a readmission review of RM_07 under the Cascade Health PPO Readmission Review Guideline (effective 03/01/2024). Cascade's guideline establishes a 30-day review window from the prior discharge and requires reviewers to determine whether the readmission diagnosis is the same as, or clinically related to, the condition treated during the prior stay (Section B1). The readmission for RM_07 occurred 5 days after discharge from MR_07, which places it within the insurer's 30-day review window (Cascade guideline: 30 days from prior discharge; discharge dates documented below). Basis for Finding: - Review window: The payer's guideline specifies a 30-day review window (Cascade Health PPO Readmission Review Guideline). The index stay ended 07/04/2026 and the readmission began 07/09/2026 (5 days later), so the readmission is within the policy window. - Clinical relationship: The readmission documentation explicitly describes RM_07 as recurrent bilateral pulmonary embolism with right femoral DVT and states that the same underlying thrombophilia (activated protein C resistance, D68.51) was identified on the index admission and drives the recurrence. The discharge summary and hospital course for RM_07 document recurrent bilateral PE and tie it directly to the index episode of thromboembolic disease treated during MR_07. - Exclusions: Cascade's Section C lists exclusions (direct transfers, scheduled admissions, SNF/LTAC/rehab discharges, AMA discharges, etc.). The record documents discharge to home with home-health and scheduled outpatient follow-up rather than any exclusion-type admission; therefore no exclusion applies. Determination and correction: Under Cascade Health PPO's Readmission Review Guideline (Section B1), because the readmission diagnosis is the same as or clinically related to the condition treated during the prior stay (recurrent pulmonary embolism related to the same underlying thrombophilia), this readmission is a Finding. This Finding will be applied in adjudication according to Cascade Health PPO's payment policy (the readmission is clinically related to the index admission and is therefore subject to the payer's rules for related readmissions). If you dispute this determination, please submit any clinical documentation that was not provided for review that specifically rebuts the documented clinical relationship between the two admissions or that establishes an applicable exclusion under Section C. Sincerely, Senior Clinical Claims Auditor Key documentation relied on (representative): - Cascade Health PPO Readmission Review Guideline (effective 03/01/2024), Section: Review Window (30 days) and Section B1 (same/related condition) and Section C (exclusions). - Readmission Discharge Summary (RM_07) - Clinical Relationship and Hospital Course documenting recurrent bilateral PE and thrombophilia present on both admissions. - Index Transfer/Discharge Summary (MR_07) - index discharge date 07/04/2026.
